findings.claim: config-ui-fidelity-gate.js's two phase() calls (phase('Render') at line 50, phase('Gate') at line 73) carry no preceding '// ---- Stage X: ... ----' banner comment, while its two sibling new workflow files landed in the same diff (subsystem-grounding.js: '// ---- Stage A/B: Ground ... ----' / '// ---- Stage C: Fold ... ----'; foreign-toolchain-pretag.js: '// ---- Stage Build: ... ----' / '// ---- Stage Gate: ... ----') both use that banner convention before every phase() call. The three files are new additions in the same commit and otherwise share an identical shape (meta.phases array, args-contract comment block, schema constants, phase()+agent() calls, null-fallback .map()), so the missing banners read as an inconsistency within the change itself rather than a deliberate omission.
findings.fix: Add '// ---- Stage Render: ... ----' and '// ---- Stage Gate: ... ----' banner comments above the two phase() calls (lines 50 and 73), matching the convention subsystem-grounding.js and foreign-toolchain-pretag.js use in the same diff.
findings.evidence: Re-read config-ui-fidelity-gate.js lines 1-102 in full and the sibling files subsystem-grounding.js and foreign-toolchain-pretag.js in full: confirmed the banner comment precedes every phase() call in both siblings but is absent at lines 50 and 73 of config-ui-fidelity-gate.js; claim survives re-check.

findings.claim: The Disposition ledger bullet's terminal-outcome enumeration now lists 7 comma-separated inline-code items in one sentence — '(`implemented`, `rejected`, `postponed`, `manual-external`, `casual-locked`, `stale`, `auto-applied`)' — after this diff inserted `casual-locked` into it; before the diff it held exactly 6 (implemented, rejected, postponed, manual-external, stale, auto-applied), the compliant maximum. RULE-SKILL-005 requires an enumeration of more than 6 comma-separated items to never sit in an inline code span or sentence — it must become a fenced block or table. This diff's own step 8, a few lines above (lines 82-91), already converts the same 9-item outcome enumeration out of a sentence into a fenced one-per-line list for exactly this reason (and matches the already-applied known finding code-style-NIT-13-r1) — the Disposition ledger bullet is the one place in this same file the diff left the now-7-item enumeration inline.
findings.fix: Convert the Disposition ledger bullet's 7-item parenthetical enumeration into a fenced one-per-line list (or a short table), the same treatment this diff already applied to the step 8 outcome enumeration a few lines above.
findings.evidence: Re-read skills/smine/smine-apply/SKILL.md line 52 and the full diff hunk adding 'casual-locked' to this line; counted 7 comma-separated inline-code items against RULE-SKILL-005's 6-item cap, and confirmed the pre-diff line (left side of the hunk) held exactly 6. Claim survives re-check.
